verdicts.argument: The two lenses agree. The materiality skeptic independently found the same FY2024 10-K p.20 sentence on Medicaid rebates and 340B ceiling prices that I used. They also showed that the reader's 62.7% government-channel share adds Part D gross spend for 2025 to Medicaid reimbursements for 2024 and divides by net sales. I re-read GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.20 and GILD:10k_FY2025.md pp.20-21, and nothing new there changes the verdict.
verdicts.correction: Keep at most one supporting line: the FY2025 10-K hardens the 340B wording to 'pervasive violations'. Give no dollar sizing.

round2.conceded: Their math critique is right, and I had not tested it. The 62.7% mixes years and mixes gross with net, and the 10% price cut is applied to all U.S. sales when the negotiated price covers Medicare only.
round2.held: Refuted as obvious. The spillover language dates to the FY2024 10-K, and the Biktarvy selection was a January 2026 headline.
round2.narrowed: Nothing to narrow. The two lenses now agree.

verdicts.argument: The materiality skeptic confirms both of my round-1 points: long-acting was already priority (ii) in FY2024 (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.38), and the deletion carries no number. They add that the $20.8B 'oral TAF' base includes Gilead's own long-acting lenacapavir, so some migration happens inside Gilead's own franchise and is not lost revenue.
verdicts.correction: At most, use the deleted sentence as a language-drift footnote.

round2.conceded: Their point that HIV $20,752M includes Sunlenca and Yeztugo, so migration to Gilead's own long-acting products is not lost revenue.
round2.held: It is still the starter thread and still not a standalone finding.

verdicts.argument: The materiality skeptic held a narrowed c03: GTN up about 250 bps to 41%, attributed to Part D. That narrowed claim is the 10-K's own sentence and table ('% of gross product sales 41 % 38 % 250 bps', 'primarily due to U.S. Medicare Part D program redesign impact', GILD:10k_FY2025.md p.41), so under this lens it is a filing headline. They also said the ~$900M was 'the analyst's number' on 2025Q3 p.12. The source says otherwise. On the grade-A 2025Q3 call, three executives stated it in prepared remarks. Daniel O'Day: 'despite the $900 million headwind for our HIV business in 2025, associated with the Medicare Part D redesign' (p.1). Johanna Mercier: 'we managed through a $900 million headwind' (p.3). Andrew Dickinson: 'we continue to expect approximately $900 million of impact to our HIV business' (p.9). The company-wide figure is also given: 'Excluding an estimated $1.1 billion in Part D Redesign headwinds, total product sales +5%' (GILD:presentations/2025Q4_earnings_slides.md p.25). The 2026 JPM slide p.5 repeats the ~$900M. So management quantified both the cause and the size of the GTN widening.
verdicts.correction: The only defensible residue is the 100 bps sensitivity (about $489M) that the materiality skeptic proposed. It is a modeling aid, not a finding the case would reward.

round2.conceded: Their point that the '$1.2B lost' overstates the loss is right: gross growth includes list increases that were never collectible, and the Veklury/Descovy mix moved the rate. That makes the reader's dollar claim weaker still.
round2.held: Refuted. Their narrowed version is the 10-K's own table and sentence, and executives quantified the cause in prepared remarks on the grade-A call. Their claim that the $900M was the analyst's number is wrong (pp.1, 3, 9).
round2.narrowed: None. This disagreement with the materiality lens remains.

verdicts.argument: The materiality skeptic holds c04 with the same corrections I made: drop the ASCENT-07 link, and note that the 10-K MD&A p.46 names the inventory build. Does an unsaid but small item clear the case bar? Here it does, narrowly. The case asks for an impact on revenue, operating income or EPS. A full write-down of the $568M (GILD:10q_2026Q2.md p.21) is about 4.3% of FY2025 non-GAAP operating income ($13,193M, proxy p.A-2). At the about 19% non-GAAP tax rate and about 1.25B shares implied by the proxy's $0.25-per-$400M, it is roughly $0.37 of EPS, or about 4.5% of $8.15. That is well above the brief's 'a few cents of EPS' rule, even as a one-time charge. In obviousness terms it is still unsaid: no release, slide or call in the index mentions the pre-commercial Trodelvy balance. The balance is shrinking ($638M in Q1 2026 to $568M in Q2 2026, 10-Q 2026Q1 p.18), so the risk may be resolving and the pitch should say so.
verdicts.correction: State it as: about $568M of Trodelvy inventory is capitalized on a manufacturing process FDA has not approved and is disclosed only in a footnote. The one-time write-down exposure is about $0.37 of EPS (about 4% of non-GAAP operating income), and the balance has declined since Q1 2026. Present it as a contingent risk, not as a trend in operating income.

round2.conceded: It is a one-time contingent charge, not a recurring hit to operating income, the H1 2026 balances are unwinding, and the 568/13,193 ratio mixes a 2026 balance with 2025 operating income.
round2.held: It holds. It is unsaid outside footnotes, and about $0.37 of EPS clears the bar.
round2.narrowed: Narrowed from a working-capital story to the Trodelvy pre-commercial footnote alone. The general inventory build is stated in the MD&A and is not a finding.

verdicts.argument: I checked the specific asymmetry: the non-GAAP figure investors get includes the IP revenue, while the pay EPS excludes it. Gilead says it plainly, and gives investors the ex-item number every time. (1) The 2026 proxy states the asymmetry in one sentence: 'In addition to exclusion of items mentioned above to arrive at non-GAAP financial information, the 2025 financial metrics further exclude: ... Previously constrained revenue related to sale of intellectual property not expected to reoccur' (GILD:companies/GILD/proxy_2026.md p.115). (2) The Q3 2025 earnings slide gives the per-share effect the reader derived: '$424M reported included a $400M nonrecurring change in revenue estimate related to a 2018 IP asset sale ... Resulted in an increase of $0.25 to both GAAP and non-GAAP EPS' (GILD:presentations/2025Q3_earnings_slides.md p.23). (3) Investors got ex-item figures each time the item appeared. Q3 2025: 'Excluding the $400 million non-recurring other revenue, non-GAAP diluted EPS would have been $2.22' (Andrew Dickinson, grade A, 2025Q3_transcript p.9). FY2025: 'Excluding acquired IPR&D, and the $400 million nonrecurring other revenue related to the IP asset sale ... operating margin was roughly 48%' (GILD:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1, grade C). Q2 2026: 'Excluding these acquisitions and the nonrecurring other revenue, non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.27' (GILD:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1, grade C). The materiality skeptic is right that the item is material, at 3.1% of non-GAAP EPS. But the candidate's claim that investors are given only the inclusive figure is false, and the asymmetry is printed in the proxy.
verdicts.correction: Nothing survives as a finding. If the team wants a footnote, it can say that Gilead's formal non-GAAP reconciliation keeps a non-recurring item that management strips out verbally every quarter. That is a presentation choice disclosed in the same documents.

round2.conceded: The math is right and the item is material: $400M is 1.4% of revenue, 3.0% of non-GAAP operating income and 3.1% of non-GAAP EPS. The formal non-GAAP reconciliation does not remove it.
round2.held: Refuted. The asymmetry is stated in the proxy (p.115), the $0.25 effect is on the Q3 2025 slide (p.23), and management gave ex-item EPS or margin on the 2025Q3, 2025Q4 and 2026Q2 calls.
round2.narrowed: My round-1 basis ('release bullet') was too thin. The kill now rests on the specific asymmetry having been said, which is a stronger reason.

verdicts.argument: The materiality skeptic adds two points, and both check against the sources. First, the October 2025 'demand-driven' remark was about 2025, when realized price fell, per the FY2025 10-K p.40. Second, the 10-Q six-month sentence reads 'Biktarvy sales increased 7% primarily due to higher demand ... and average realized price' (GILD:10q_2026Q2.md p.33). So the claimed reversal comes from picking one quarter's sentence. Together with my round-1 evidence (slide p.9, call script, release), the candidate is both said plainly and overstated.

round2.conceded: The year-mixing and quarter-picking points, which I had not raised.
round2.held: Fatal. Management said it in Q2 2026 prepared remarks and on the slide.

verdicts.argument: The two lenses agree. The materiality skeptic shows the $35M figure attributes ViiV's Apretude price increase to Gilead. Gilead's own drift is about $6M, or 0.02% of revenue. Together with management's statement that PrEP realized price is rising (GILD:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1), the 'discounting' thesis fails on both lenses.
verdicts.correction: Use the label asymmetry only in the product comparison.

round2.conceded: The misattribution of the relative price gap, and their point that early payment limits are set from WAC.

verdicts.argument: I am changing this verdict. In round 1 it passed on obviousness: the August 2025 widening appears in no release, slide or call. The case bar has two parts, though: 'material (big enough to change an investor's view) and not obvious'. The materiality skeptic's figure of about $29.9M per 1,000 patients, about 0.1% of revenue, has no sourced patient count behind it, and part of it may be patients already on Biktarvy off-label. An unsaid finding that small does not change an investor's view, so it should not take a row in the findings table. It stays the best fine-print evidence for the product comparison, where the case asks for label differences whether or not they are large.
verdicts.correction: Move it from the findings table to the product comparison, as the lead label edge (v19 to v22 indication) framed as share defense ahead of the 2028 negotiated price.

round2.conceded: It is too small and unsized to count as a material finding. Being unsaid does not rescue a finding worth about 0.1% of revenue.
round2.held: It is still the least obvious item in the set: no press release and no call mention.
round2.narrowed: From a held finding to product-section evidence only.

verdicts.argument: Per the coordinator's note, a GILD-only row in policy_exposure.csv means the other companies' rows are not in the table yet. My round-1 refutation did not rely on the table. The materiality skeptic wrote that 'a search of FY2025 peer 10-Ks found no equivalent disclosure'. That is wrong. MRK:10k_FY2025.md p.54 says Merck 'agreed to repatriate and share with the Federal government a portion of foreign revenue received by the Company as a result of the government's successful trade policy efforts', and MRK 10-Q 2026Q1 p.30 and 10-Q 2026Q2 p.32 repeat it. The White House fact sheet says 'The agreements require the nine companies to repatriate increased foreign revenue on existing products' (policy_gov:policy_gov/wh/wh_fact_sheet_2025-12-19_nine_deals_mrk_bmy_amgn_gild.md p.1), and those nine include Merck, BMS and Amgen. The materiality skeptic also correctly notes that force_summary.csv lists Merck's Keytruda as an expected 2027 selection worth 48.7% of Merck revenue, quoting Merck's own 10-K. So Gilead's single-drug concentration is not unique either.
verdicts.correction: Drop the uniqueness claims. Biktarvy at 48.7% of revenue is context for the starter thread and is matched by Keytruda at Merck.

round2.conceded: Their corrections that ABBV is 22.5% in force_summary.csv, not 16.9%, and that Keytruda's expected selection matches the 48.7%. Their point that the repatriation term is conditional and returns a portion of an increase, so it cannot cut current revenue.
round2.held: Fatal. The repatriation term is not unique: Merck's 10-K and the White House fact sheet show it, so their narrowed 'only shortlist 10-K disclosing it' is wrong.

verdicts.argument: Both lenses agree: Biktarvy is the right product, and the c08 label widening is its least obvious edge but unsized. Moving c08 out of the findings table makes it the lead row of the product comparison.
verdicts.correction: Lead with the v19 to v22 indication change and frame it as share defense.

round2.conceded: Its dollar effect is not shown.
round2.held: It is a valid fine-print edge that no Gilead release or call states.

overall: After round 2, only c04, narrowed to the footnote-only $568M Trodelvy pre-commercial inventory (about $0.37 of EPS one-time), is both unsaid and big enough. c05 is material but its specific asymmetry is printed in the proxy and stripped out verbally on every call, and c08 is unsaid but too small, so it moves to the product section. The main disagreements with the materiality lens are c03 and c05, where the sources show management quantified and stated each point itself.
